title: Conceptual framework of acoustic comfort design enablers for a classroom: A systematic review
review_question: RQ1: What design enablers must be considered in ensuring the acoustical performance of a classroom? RQ2: How do the acoustic parameters respond to different design enablers in a classroom?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Inclusion: English language, peer-reviewed, original research articles, containing keywords (classroom acoustics, acoustic performance, acoustic conditions, acoustic parameters), full text availability, in-field measurement, computer simulation, calculation prediction. Exclusion: Duplication, non-English language, review articles, incomplete files, irrelevant topic/title, unavailability of full text, irrelevant research aim/outcomes.

synthesis_conclusions: Acoustic comfort in classrooms is influenced by six design enablers: material, volume, layout, amplification system, noise, and occupancy, categorized as physical, human, and noise attributes.
The most crucial enabler for acoustic comfort is the application of finished materials, with types and configurations significantly determining acoustic conditions.
Noise disruption from indoor (HVAC, student activity) and outdoor sources degrades acoustic comfort, affecting comprehension and attention.
Classroom layout (seating arrangement, student-teacher distance) influences acoustic performance.
Volume, occupancy, and amplification systems also impact the classroom acoustic environment.
Reverberation time (RT) is notably impacted by surface materials and ceiling height.
Speech Transmission Index (STI) primarily depends on noise levels, layout, and amplification system.
Speech clarity (C50) is influenced by classroom layout (hearing distance) and material enablers.
Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) is substantially impacted by noise, amplification systems, and occupancy.
evidence_gaps: Shortage of thorough reviews examining the impact of design factors in predicting acoustic quality.
Limited number of studies and insignificant impact observed for some acoustic parameters, leading to their exclusion from the conceptual framework.
Future research should comprehensively analyze several design enablers and acoustical parameters that have not been adequately evaluated and demand more investigation.
Review primarily focuses on traditional classroom design, potentially overlooking alternative designs like smart or hybrid classrooms and laboratories.
limitations: The study encompasses only three databases (Science Direct, Scopus, Google Scholar) to identify research articles.
The review period is limited from 1995 until the end of December 2023.
The review primarily focuses on traditional classroom design and may overlook alternative classroom designs (smart, hybrid, laboratories).

theory_commitments.specific_claim: This paper proposes a novel conceptual framework that identifies and structures design enablers for achieving acoustic comfort in classroom environments, synthesized from a systematic review of existing literature.
